national.title: Ukraine says bodycam video shows deadly Russian double-tap bombing
national.summary: At least 40 people were killed and another 30 may still be under the rubble after Monday's attack on a Ukrainian village, Kyiv says.
national.body:
A bodycam video has been released by Ukraine police they say shows the moments between two powerful Russian bomb strikes that killed at least 40 people at an aid centre and a shelter.

The footage, from a camera on one of the killed police officers, shows residents of the southern village of Kamyshuvakha going to an underground shelter after the first attack on Monday. Soon after a blast is heard and flames are seen as the shelter is hit.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said more than 30 people may still be under the rubble, as a search operation continued for the third day.

Nine gliding bombs, some weighing 3,000kg, hit the village as people had gathered to get humanitarian aid, Ukraine said.

The bodycam footage was released by Ukraine's national police on Wednesday.

It shows huge devastation after the first bomb strike on the village in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, as shocked local residents stare at the rubble.

A voice of a military official is then heard on a two-way radio warning police on the ground of more glide bombs being launched towards Kamyshuvakha.

"Quickly [go] to the shelter!" one of the police officers tells local residents, who are seen walking into the shelter - at least two floors underground.

national.title: Mississippi Senate race is toss-up, with margin of under 50 votes
national.summary: The Senate race in deep-red Mississippi remains unresolved Wednesday morning, as Democrat Scott Colom has mounted a surprisingly competitive challenge to incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith.
national.body: Washington — The Senate midterm race in deep-red Mississippi remains unresolved Wednesday morning, with Democrat Scott Colom mounting a surprisingly competitive challenge to incumbent GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith. With 96% of the vote in, just a few dozen votes separated the candidates, a stunningly close result in the Magnolia State.Hyde-Smith, 67, has been in the Senate since 2018 and is seeking reelection. But Colom, a district attorney, launched a formidable challenge, and could deliver Democrats yet another victory. Democrats saw a slew of wins in Senate races Tuesday night, including in states that President Trump won by double digits in the 2024 elections. With more than four flips of GOP-held seats, Democrats secured enough seats to take control of the chamber in the new year. If Colom manages to pull off a victory, he would add to their majority. Colom, 43, is a seventh-generation Mississippian who campaigned on cost of living and health care issues. Democrats began investing in the race in recent weeks, seeing an opportunity for a pickup. But the possible outcome still appeared exceedingly unlikely heading into Election Day.Mr. Trump won Mississippi by 20 points in 2024, and the state hasn't elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1982. Speaking to supporters in the wee hours of the morning on Wednesday, Colom said, "The results are all trending in our direction.""We are trending in counties that people thought we had no chance to compete in," Colom said. "And we're winning them."The unresolved race in Mississippi comes as Alaska's Senate race is also outstanding, leaving the size of Democrats' majority up in the air.

national.title: Back in the majority, Democrats have plans for a long list of Trump investigations
national.summary: Democrats will have the ability to subpoena records and compel individuals to testify. The Epstein files, Elon Musk, the Iran war and Trump's business interests may all come under the microscope.
national.body:
Democrats won big in the midterm elections, but with President Trump still in the White House, the next Congress is unlikely to see much major legislation signed into law.

Instead, expect to see a lot more oversight. With public corruption and failing leadership as two of the top issues concerning voters, congressional Democrats have an ambitious agenda of investigations planned for their return to power in the House and Senate.

Their new majorities mean that they will have at their disposal the full investigatory powers of the Congress, which include the ability to subpoena records for review and compel individuals to testify before lawmakers.

Elections Democrats win full control of Congress, ushering in a new era of divided government Rep. Robert Garcia, the California Democrat who is expected to become chair of the House Oversight committee, put it bluntly in a statement: "LAWYER UP."

The Democratic Party has a long list of investigative targets. According to conversations with Democratic House and Senate committee staffers, here are some areas the party is likely to prioritize in its oversight work.

Among Democrats' primary targets: the administration's handling of — and connections to — the scandals of late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. Bipartisan congressional action forced the Trump administration to release extensive documents tied to federal investigations of Epstein's crimes and other alleged offenses, though Democrats maintain that many of the records were improperly redacted or withheld from the public. They also say that the Justice Department has worked to shield Trump from damaging allegations — claims that the department's leadership has denied.

In the new Congress, lawmakers are expected to probe ties between Epstein and other powerful figures, including the president himself, which they say is part of an effort to secure accountability for victims of Epstein's crimes.

In connection with an October report , Rep. Jamie Raskin of Maryland, the top Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, said, "Donald Trump says he knew Jeffrey Epstein 'just like everybody in Palm Beach knew him.' Not exactly."

national.title: Iranian leaders say midterm results show U.S. voters have rejected Trump's war
national.summary: Concerns about the war, particularly frustration over rising prices for fuel and other goods in the U.S., helped Democrats win control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday's vote, a sharp setback for President Donald Trump and his Republican Party.
national.body:
Elena Becatoros, Associated Press Elena Becatoros, Associated Press

Iranians on Wednesday struck a defiant tone, celebrating U.S. voters' rebuke of President Donald Trump in the midterm elections while many in the Middle East waited to see how the results could affect the Iran war.

Concerns about the war, particularly frustration over rising prices for fuel and other goods in the U.S., helped Democrats win control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday's vote, a sharp setback for Trump and his Republican Party.

But Iran's supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, whose father and predecessor was killed in the opening strikes of the war in February, dismissed the prospect of any major change in the U.S. approach to the Islamic Republic.

Stand with free and independent journalism. Join Press Pass from PBS News

"If there are still those who harbor even a slight hope for a change in behavior or partisan and factional shifts within the system of domination, or who imagine that by giving concessions to America they can dissuade it from hostility toward the Iranian nation, they are gravely mistaken," he said on his social media account.

The broader region has been on edge for weeks over the prospect of the U.S. resuming full-scale military operations against Iran. Talks aimed at preventing renewed fighting are continuing, while other U.S. allies in the region urge Washington against resuming a war that began more than eight months ago and has rattled the global economy and devastated Iran.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has reportedly pushed for more strikes, while Trump has alternated between threatening major military action and pushing for a deal.

national.title: When is life insurance taxable?
national.summary: Life insurance isn't usually taxable, but there are some occasions when you or your heirs may wind up with a bill.
national.body: Life insurance can be a game-changer, providing much-needed financial support when a loved one dies. But many beneficiaries often wonder if that money comes with a tax burden.In most cases, it doesn't, as the payout is not considered a part of the beneficiary's taxable income. There are some rare instances in which you may owe taxes on a life insurance payout, though.Below, we'll break down what you need to know about the taxability of life insurance and what it may mean for you and your loved ones.Find out more about your life insurance options online now.Are life insurance proceeds taxable?Life insurance proceeds aren't typically considered income for a beneficiary, so if someone receives a lump-sum policy payout after a loved one's passing, it usually isn't taxable. That noted, this isn't uniform and there are multiple instances in which you may receive a tax bill alongside a life insurance payout. Some instances in which life insurance may be taxable include:You received the payout in installmentsIf a beneficiary's payout is done in installments over time, they may owe taxes on certain interest payments if they exceed the policy's paid value. This might happen if the policy has earned interest, for example.Explore the life insurance policies available to you today.You make a cash withdrawal from your policy. Permanent life insurance policies have a cash value that you may be able to withdraw from once it reaches a certain point. These withdrawals are generally taxable if they exceed what you've already paid in premiums.You surrender or sell your policy.If you give up your life insurance policy in exchange for cash, the money you receive for the policy in excess of your premiums must be reported as income and is therefore taxable. Your employer–provided benefits exceed $50,000.If your employer provides life insurance coverage that's over $50,000, you will be taxed on the cost of the excess coverage, minus any portion you already paid toward the policy.You received interest from your policy.Some life insurance policies earn interest and grow in value over time. national.title: US midterm results a 'victory' for Canadians hopeful of tariff relief
national.summary: With Canada-US trade talks back on, Tuesday’s midterm Democratic wave puts pressure on the White House to come to a deal.
national.body:
It was the midterm result that many in Canada had hoped for - a Democratic sweep that was in part a repudiation by American voters of Donald Trump's tariff on close trade allies.

"I was doing cartwheels down the street," said Ontario Premier Doug Ford on Wednesday morning, calling it "a victory for Canada".

Tuesday night's result is unlikely to grant Canada relief from those tariffs any time soon, but there is anticipation that the political shifts could create a more favourable environment for Ottawa to get the best deal now that on-again-off-again trade talks are back on.

US voters cited affordability as a main concern heading into the midterms and a survey by the Cato Institute in September , external suggested that about 75% believe the tariffs have raised prices.

In states like Maine and Michigan, tariffs played a significant role in the hard-fought races.

In Maine, incumbent Republican Senator Susan Collins clashed with the White House over tariffs.

She successfully lobbied to have some duties that directly affected the state removed, including on road salt, refrigeration equipment and seaweed, but in the end lost to Democrat Troy Jackson.

A similar story played out in Michigan, where state's the automobile manufacturing industry is deeply intertwined with Canada's - and where Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers.

national.title: Iran's chief negotiator says Americans voted 'no to war'
national.summary: "We endorse this message," Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf says, as Donald Trump acknowledges the conflict's role in the Republican Party's defeat.
national.body:
Iran's chief negotiator in talks with the US has said that Americans voted "NO TO WAR", after President Donald Trump's Republican Party suffered a stunning defeat in the midterm elections.

"We endorse this message," parliament speaker Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf wrote on X.

"If the US [government] betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare," he warned.

Trump acknowledged on Tuesday that the poor results for Republican congressional candidates were partly due to the war and the related surge in petrol prices. But he insisted that he did not regret launching a joint attack with Israel on Iran in February.

In an interview with Fox News, Trump said of the midterm results: "I think a part of it was Iran".

He went on to say: "People agree with what I'm doing on Iran but they really probably weren't willing to do the short term consequences of paying more for gasoline - I understand that."

Speaking separately to the BBC's US news partner, CBS News, Trump said the conflict would end "when I say it ends".

In recent weeks, Trump has warned that the US and Israel could return to all-out war after the midterms if a deal to end the conflict cannot be reached with Iran.

national.title: Trump asking advisers if Hegseth should go, sources say
national.summary: President Trump has been asking his advisers if Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth should remain in his job after Tuesday's losses.
national.body: Washington â President Trump has been asking advisers around him and on the phone whether Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth should stay in his job, following Republicans' catastrophic losses Tuesday night, multiple sources familiar with the matter tell CBS News. Some White House aides have predicted some of the blame for GOP midterm losses will be trained on Adm. Brad Cooper, the head of U.S. Central Command, and Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen. Dan Caine, who both played big roles in guidance on the Iran war.Still, other sources said the president hasn't decided to replace Hegseth. Before the election, Democrats were already trying to impeach Hegseth, and the likelihood of an impeachment effort could increase with Democrats holding strong majorities in both chambers. Vice President JD Vance is blaming the war for the GOP defeat. "The reason we lost is the war," he said in a lengthy post on X Wednesday morning. One source told CBS News that GOP Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis is being floated as a possible replacement for Hegseth, arguing DeSantis could go through Senate confirmation in the lame-duck period and then take the post when his term as governor expires Jan. 5. Asked for comment about reports that Hegseth's future as defense secretary, White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly said in a statement that Mr. Trump "has full confidence in Secretary Hegseth." In the statement, Kelly also praised the military operations in Iran and Venezuela and Hegseth's efforts to reverse the Biden Pentagon's prioritizing of "DEI and woke ideology."

national.title: Johnson won't seek reelection as House speaker after Republican wipeout
national.summary: It's a swift rise and fall for Mike Johnson, often seen as an accidental speaker, who nevertheless drew close to President Donald Trump and led the House GOP during a tumultuous era, with one of the slimmest majorities in modern times.
national.body:
Lisa Mascaro, Associated Press Lisa Mascaro, Associated Press

WASHINGTON (AP) — House Speaker Mike Johnson will be stepping aside from Republican Party leadership after the GOP's wipeout in the midterm election, declining to seek support to stay on as House minority leader in the new Congress, according to two people familiar with his decision Wednesday.

Johnson is expected to retain his seat as a rank-and-file member of the House from Louisiana when the Congress convenes in January. He won reelection from his Shreveport-area district for an eighth term in office.

It's a swift rise and fall for Johnson, often seen as an accidental speaker, who nevertheless drew close to President Donald Trump and led the House GOP during a tumultuous era, with one of the slimmest majorities in modern times. And it sets up a fierce internal party battle for the new GOP leader after Democrats swept to power.

Johnson's sunny assertions that Republicans would defy history in the midterms, as voters traditionally have punished the president's party in power, failed to hold. Instead, Republicans were trounced as Democrats swept to the House majority, leaving Johnson without a path to power.

The people who told The Associated Press about Johnson's decision insisted on anonymity to disclose it.

national.title: 'Most difficult days of my life' for keeper Owono
national.summary: FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono puts out a statement through his club, expressing his sorrow and pain after Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel's death.
national.body:
FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono says he is experiencing "the most difficult days of my life" after the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.

Tenerife player De Miguel, 30, died after suffering a serious injury in a collision with Owono during a Spanish second division match on Monday.

The world of football has paid tribute to De Miguel, a father-of-one who joined Tenerife in summer 2025, with a minute's silence being held at all games in European competition this week.

Owono's club issued a statement on the goalkeeper's behalf on Wednesday, explaining the 25-year-old "wishes to share a few words personally".

"These are the most difficult days of my life," Owono says in the statement.

"I struggle to find the words, and it is very hard for me to come to terms with what has happened.

"I feel enormous pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him.

"I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are all experiencing.

national.title: Frantic 911 call from hero dad who killed school shooter released
national.summary: The armed father who was hailed for his heroic actions​ during a deadly shooting​ at his daughters' elementary school in Oregon frantically called authorities before he went after the shooter.
national.body: The armed father who was hailed for his heroic actions during a deadly shooting at his daughters' elementary school in Oregon frantically called authorities before he went after the shooter, according to a recording of the 911 call released Tuesday."Someone's at the school, at my daughters' school with a gun. I have a gun, and I will shoot them right now if I have to," 36-year-old Kaylub Giamanco told the 911 dispatcher as the Oct. 15 shooting was beginning to unfold.Giamanco's two daughters were inside Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, when he happened to drive by the school and see the shooter begin his rampage. Giamanco's girls survived the attack.The shooter killed three children, ages 5, 8 and 11, and a 25-year-old teacher. Giamanco killed the 16-year-old shooter after rushing into the school with his handgun.The roughly 80-second-long recording released Tuesday captures the initial chaos surrounding the shooting, which started when the gunman shot at a vehicle. Giamanco previously told Oregon Public Broadcasting he went for his gun in a panic after he saw the shooter throw his weapon over the school's fence and then climb after it.Giamanco's first words on the 911 call were, "Oh my God."After Giamanco described the situation to the dispatcher, the dispatcher asked exactly what happened."Silver Rail Elementary! Silver Rail Elementary!" Giamanco told her.The dispatcher asked Giamanco for his phone number and then if he knew who the shooter was."This is my daughters' school. I'm about to go kill this kid," Giamanco said.The dispatcher asked again if he knew the shooter's identity."No, I don't f---ing know, I was just driving," Giamanco said.Giamanco then told the dispatcher the shooter was inside the school. The dispatcher asked where. Giamanco again gave the name of the school. national.title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms
national.summary: For some young Africans, these victories offer a glimpse of what a new generation of voters could do at home.
national.body:
It was an unlikely greeting to hear at a Democratic Party victory rally after the US midterm elections.

Abdul El-Sayed , 42, born to Egyptian immigrant parents, playfully addressed Vice-President JD Vance, who had campaigned against him but will now swear him into office in January as Michigan's new Senator.

The US-born Democrat spent much of his campaign fending off attacks from conservative media and President Donald Trump, who accused him of supporting the Muslim Brotherhood. El-Sayed rejected the allegations.

"My name is Abdul Rahman Mohammed El-Sayed," he said in an Egyptian Arabic accent to the cheering crowd at his victory rally. His Arabic Muslim name was a target for many of his opponents. He is set to become the first Muslim senator.

El-Sayed ran a social media-first campaign, with TikTok edits showing him speaking directly to young voters, tapping into Gen Z humour, and sporting friendship bracelets.

The former public health administrator's campaign centred on a progressive agenda, including Medicare for All, affordable housing and curbing corporate influence in politics. He has also been a vocal critic of US military aid to Israel.

But El-Sayed was not alone. From an Ethiopian-born Gen Z congresswoman to candidates with Nigerian heritage, several other politicians with African roots won in this year's midterms.

The elections, held halfway through a president's four-year term, decide who represents Americans in Congress, as well as in thousands of state and local offices.

national.title: How Trump and Republicans lost the 2026 midterm elections, according to AP Voter Poll
national.summary: After more than a decade with Donald Trump at the epicenter of U.S. politics, most voters appear exhausted and exasperated by him, according to The AP Voter Poll, a survey of midterm voters in all 50 states.
national.body:
Humera Lodhi, Associated Press Humera Lodhi, Associated Press

WASHINGTON (AP) — After more than a decade with Donald Trump at the epicenter of U.S. politics, most voters appear exhausted and exasperated by him, according to The AP Voter Poll, a survey of midterm voters in all 50 states.

The president's failure to deliver on key promises — most prominently, his vows to tame inflation, which has worsened instead — clearly weighed on his fellow Republicans in Tuesday's midterm elections for the House and the Senate. The polling shows that voters generally saw Trump as being more focused on his own fortune and gold-leafed existence than their needs.

The president also helped elevate candidates with obvious flaws, amplifying their struggles in an already challenging year. He suggested in a Tuesday evening interview with Fox News Channel that Democrats "fought hard" and that the Republican base "didn't like the candidates" he had endorsed because some of his picks were not fully loyal to him.

Stand with free and independent journalism. Join Press Pass from PBS News

But the poll also contains a serious note of caution for Democrats. Many voters dislike the party — and while Democrats hold an advantage on key issues such as the economy, their edge is relatively slim. About 7 in 10 voters said Congress is not doing enough to provide checks and balances for the president, setting the bar for Democrats who won back the Senate and the House.

It was impossible for GOP candidates to hide from inflation. Voters could see it clearly in their receipts from grocery stores and gasoline stations. The financial blow of an auto repair or a utility bill after a sweltering summer was inescapable. And even in Republican strongholds such as Texas, the drag caused by inflation helped Democrats.

national.body: Washington — The Senate race in Alaska remains unresolved Wednesday, as a contest that has garnered widespread attention over the two candidates named Dan Sullivan faces a lengthy ballot-counting process.Incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan and Democrat Mary Peltola are facing off in the race, which also has two other candidates on the ballot: an independent candidate and retired teacher Daniel J. Sullivan, and another Republican, Gerald Heikes.With around three-quarters of the vote in as of Wednesday morning, the race remains a toss-up, according to CBS News estimates. The count in Alaska could stretch on. Alaska has a ranked-choice voting system, which allows voters to rank as many or as few candidates as they'd like in order of preference. If no candidate secures support from more than 50% of voters as their top choice, the count goes to a second round. The ranked-choice tabulation doesn't occur until the last counting of ballots 15 days after Election Day, meaning the process could drag on for weeks if one candidate does not secure more than 50% of first-place support on the ballot.The results in Alaska will come after Democrats already secured enough seats to take control of the Senate, winning in several states that President Trump won by double digits in 2024. Alaska could either add to the Democrats' majority, or deliver some relief to Republicans by blunting additional Democratic gains. One other Senate contest, the Mississippi race, also remained unresolved Wednesday morning. Speaking to reporters early Wednesday morning, Peltola said, "The results are not going to be fast." "But Alaskans are patient," she said. "We just want to make sure the folks [in] the Lower 48 know it won't be hours, it won't be days, it will be weeks." Sen. national.body:
Hungary has opened communist-era secret police files to the public, in a controversial move the government says will help Hungarian society heal itself from the traumas of 45 years of communist rule.

Critics say the move comes too late, that the files themselves are incomplete, and that the move risks sowing division and causing unnecessary anguish to family members.

The date of the opening is symbolic - on 4 November 1956 Soviet tanks rolled through Budapest and other cities, to crush Hungary's short-lived revolution.

"I ask everyone to treat this long overdue publication of documents with dignity and humanity," Prime Minister Péter Magyar told reporters at the state archives in Budapest.

"Many families will now face difficult information, often related to a deceased relative," he added. "It is impossible to process a trauma without discussion and asking questions."

Magyar defended the move, which was a central promise of his election campaign ahead of his landslide victory in April elections, as the fulfilment of a promise made by those who toppled the Communist party in 1989 in Hungary.

"This achievement marks an unprecedented diplomatic initiative by an American First Lady", it added.

Both the Russian and Ukrainian sides repeatedly thanked Melania Trump for brokering the ceasefire, though neither elaborated on the nature or extent of her involvement.

local.title: A big night for Democrats
local.summary: At the local, state, and national level, Democrats made major victories, flipping seats and incumbents handily defeating challengers.
local.body:
Monroe County Democratic candidates won big Tuesday evening, mirroring a national trend and signaling the local Republican party's dwindling influence.

According to unofficial election night results, all incumbent Democratic candidates for local state Senate and Assembly seats, as well as Congressman Joe Morelle, handily won reelection against their Republican challengers. Gov. Kathy Hochul secured a second term in office after facing a challenge from Republican Bruce Blakeman. Meanwhile, Democrats flipped several key local seats long held by Republicans.

At the national level, Democrats appeared poised to take control of both the House of Representatives and Senate, in what appears to be a rebuke of President Donald Trump's policies in his second term in office.

"It's a historic night," Morelle said. "Americans showed up, and I think they had to make a decision on the direction of this government and the direction of this country. They spoke loudly, they spoke clearly, in an overwhelming way, rejected the politics of hatred and divisiveness and corruption. And I couldn't be prouder."

Morelle said his key focuses will be putting an end to stock trading for Congressmembers and Supreme Court Justices and attempting to quell the influence of "dark money" in the House.

Attendees at the celebration party for Monroe County Democrats at the Hyatt Regency in Rochester saw a chance for change.

"One thing I hope, really hope, is that Democrats and Republicans can come together and make good decisions," said Janis White, a party supporter. "...Just come together and make good decisions for the United States."

Some Democrats scored major upsets for seats that have historically been held tightly by the GOP. Republican Gates Town Supervisor Cosmo Giunta, first elected in 2018, lost to Democrat Nick Coffee, who appears to be the first Democrat elected to lead Gates in the town's history.

local.body:
The Fredonia Shakespeare Club welcomed Elizabeth Cady Stanton back at the home of Mary Croxton during its recent meeting.

The Fredonia Censor first recorded Elizabeth Cady Stanton's visit on April 27, 1870. Mrs. Elizabeth C. Stanton (the name she used instead of Mrs. Henry Stanton) was on a Lyceum tour around the country.

The Censor wrote: "The beautiful weather of Saturday, April 23 made it pleasant for an attendance from the surrounding towns, and consequence was a house full of auditors to greet the great advocate of the cause of her sex. Not one was disappointed." The name of the lecture was "Open the Door." ... The argument of the lecture was strong and varied with flashes of wit, pathos and eloquence that retained the unwearied attention of the audience till the close of the two hours...most were unable to deny the brilliancy of the effort as a literary production."

Stanton gave this advice to the girls; "not to marry till they are twenty-five, for they are not fully developed mentally or physically till then. "Women must learn to depend upon themselves. Irving's picture of a stately oak, covered with a clinging vine...when the lightning strikes the oak, or the woodman's axe levels it to the ground, the vine dies with it and there the simile ends. Many a family's dependence is thus stricken down, leaving the mother with not only herself, but a half a dozen children to look out for, and the speaker exhorted the young girls to prepare themselves for such emergencies, instead of expecting and making themselves fit for nothing but "to twine."

E.C. Stanton gave a capital plea, for allowing women on juries, and gave a scathing denunciation of the abominable proceedings allowed in courts when women are on trial, also a review of the old laws of 1848 in reference to the rights of women to their own property and children. She advised the women not to pay taxes till they could have representatives. She went on claiming that the old text of "Wives, obey your Husbands," was of no more authority now than "Honor the King."

She proclaimed that women's suffrage is the paramount issue at present, just as she did in July 1848 at the first Women's Rights Convention in Seneca Falls, New York. Her Declaration of Sentiments: We hold these truths to be self-evident: that all men and women are created equal, that they are endowed by their Creator with certain inalienable rights, that among these are life, liberty, and pursuit of happiness; that to secure these rights governments are instituted, deriving their just powers from the consent of the governed."

local.title: The rut Is coming: best days for deer hunters
local.summary: As November arrives, deer hunters across Chautauqua County and Western New York are entering one of the most anticipated stretches of the whitetail season. The woods are changing, the days are growing shorter and the excitement is building. The best part of deer season may be just around the corner.
local.body:
As November arrives, deer hunters across Chautauqua County and Western New York are entering one of the most anticipated stretches of the whitetail season. The woods are changing, the days are growing shorter and the excitement is building. The best part of deer season may be just around the corner.

The annual whitetail rut, when bucks focus much of their attention on finding receptive does, can turn an ordinary day in the woods into an unforgettable hunt. During the chase phase, bucks begin searching for does that have not yet entered estrus. They travel more widely, follow fresh scent trails and sometimes appear in places where hunters have seen little daytime activity. As more does become receptive, buck movement can intensify, creating some of the season's most exciting opportunities.

For hunters, this is the time to stay alert, remain patient and make every sit count. A buck that has been moving mostly after dark may suddenly appear in daylight, following a doe through a hedgerow, crossing a field edge or slipping through a familiar patch of timber. Scrapes and rubs can offer clues to deer activity locations, but nothing compares with being in the woods when the rut is in full swing.

The timing of the rut varies from year to year and across individual areas, so there is no guaranteed peak day. Still, early to mid-November is traditionally a prime time period to watch for increased buck movement in Western New York.

According to experts, the rut is triggered by the photoperiod, like many things in nature. That is simply the ratio of daytime hours to nighttime hours. Experts say it is not affected by temperature or other weather factors, so say many experts. According to the onX app, the seeking phase of the rut started Halloween weekend and runs through Nov. 7, then chasing Nov. 8-12, then the peak rut Nov. 13-17. The post rut in Western New York will likely occur during the start of the firearm season, Nov. 18-28. Get out your calendars. On the other hand, you gotta go into the woods when you can. We all have different schedules and time in the woods is priceless. Just do go prepared with tick protection.

For archery hunters, the timing can be especially exciting. New York's Southern Zone early bowhunting season runs through Nov. 20, putting hunters in the woods during the best part of the rut. A well-timed encounter with a mature buck at close range is what keeps bowhunters returning season after season. With the wind in their favor, careful silent access to a stand and willingness to sit through changing conditions, hunters may find that their patience pays off.

local.body:
Pictured is the site of the proposed concrete and asphalt recycling yard owned and operated by Steve St. George.

OBSERVER Photos by Braden Carmen Steve St. George submitted plans for a concrete and asphalt recycling yard to be located at his operational property located in the town of Pomfret.

After three separate meetings with the Town of Pomfret Zoning Board of Appeals, Steve St. George was still without a permit for a concrete and asphalt recycling yard to be allowed at a property he owns in the town.

St. George sought a special use permit to establish a concrete and asphalt recycling yard at 3624 Webster Road, Fredonia. This property, formerly used for grape vineyards, is listed on the tax map as SBL:131.00-1-51.2. The property is zoned Agricultural/Residential (AR1).

St. George operates S. St. George Enterprises, a construction company that often works with roadways in the region. St. George is seeking a permit to recycle the materials from his company on site. St. George Enterprises operates six days a week, with Saturday hours limited 8 a.m. to noon. Operations are scaled back during the winter.

Initially, a building permit at the site was denied because the use was not defined under the zoning code's acceptable uses. That meant a special use permit was necessary for the project to proceed. The Zoning Board is required to evaluate the project under the State Environmental Quality Review Act guidelines.

Five members of the Board attended the recent meeting, with alternate Jonathan Townsend sitting in for Ruth Eckstrom. Code Enforcement Officer Warren Kelly was also in attendance.

After public opposition of the project in September from roughly a dozen guests, including seven members of the public that spoke on the matter, St. George sat alone in the audience at the latest meeting.

The team did not provide any further details in announcing the move in a statement, though the le
local.body:
ORCHARD PARK -- The Buffalo Bills released veteran safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson on Tuesday, a day after he completed his one-game NFL suspension for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players.

The team did not provide any further details in announcing the move in a statement, though the league discipline and Gardner-Johnson’s inconsistent performance were considered to play contributing factors.

Coach Joe Brady was non-committal regarding Gardner-Johnson’s status with the team when the NFL issued its suspension as the Bills entered their bye week off two weeks ago. And he sidestepped a question regarding the player on Monday, a day after Buffalo improved to 6-1 following a 36-10 win over Baltimore.

Brady would only say he had no discussions with Gardner-Johnson after the player returned to attend meetings. The NFL also granted the Bills a one-day exemption to carry an additional player through Tuesday.

The team is off until Thursday, when Buffalo resumes practice to prepare to play at Minnesota (6-1) on Monday night.

The 28-year-old signed a one-year contract with the Bills in March, with Buffalo becoming Gardner-Johnson’s sixth stop in five seasons, including two separate stints in Philadelphia. Though he won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Eagles, the eighth-year NFL player arrived in Buffalo with an established reputation of being a noted trash-talker and as someone who has on occasion crossed the line with illegal hits.

GM Brandon Beane acknowledged he consulted with coaches and had a lengthy discussion with Gardner-Johnson regarding his reputation before signing him.

Gardner-Johnson’s play was in question even before he was ejected for spitting during a post-whistle confrontation in a 33-30 win at Las Vegas on Oct. 18. He started six games at safety and was part of a secondary that was among the NFL’s worst against the pass.

local.body:
It’s been a confusing college football season so far. Nobody felt that more deeply than the College Football Playoff selection committee, which raised eyebrows aplenty in its first attempt of the season to make sense of it all.

Undefeated Miami received top billing in the committee’s opening crack at the CFP rankings Tuesday, followed by Georgia (7-1) and undefeated Utah.

From there, the 13 people in that room could have been picking from a hat. Defending champion Indiana (8-1) was ranked fourth -- eight spots ahead of Ohio State (6-2), which beat the Hoosiers 19-15 last month but has since lost quarterback Julian Sayin (to say nothing of another game).

At No. 5 was Alabama (6-2) -- eight spots ahead of Tennessee (6-2), even though the Tide is only a few weeks removed from a 16-point loss to the Vols. At No. 6 was Kentucky (7-1), followed by Texas (6-2).

UCLA, the nation’s only other undefeated team, was ranked eighth.

Oh, and Notre Dame. The Irish (7-1) were ranked 11th -- seven spots lower than their spot in the AP Top 25 -- and that ranking brought with it a simple message: As the last team that would make the bracket if the playoffs started today, they need to beat Miami on Saturday or risk slipping due to a schedule that clearly did not impress the committee.

“A very, very good football team,” committee chair Hunter Yurachek said of Notre Dame. “But when you look at Notre Dame’s schedule and the wins they have versus the teams ahead of them, they don’t have that signature win right now.”

In fact, Notre Dame’s biggest game so far resulted in its only loss -- 28-24 at BYU on Oct. 17.

local.title: Locals win re-election to state Senate as Democrats widen majority
local.summary: Voters return Cooney, Brouk, Ort and Helming in regional races.
local.body:
Democrats took back the supermajority Tuesday in the New York state Senate and were poised for additional gains as final results roll in.

Locally, though, the balance of power stayed unchanged Tuesday, as incumbent Democratic Sens. Jeremy Cooney and Samra Brouk won re-election, as did Minority Leader Rob Ort and Republican Sen. Pam Helming.

State Democrats entered the night with a 41-22 advantage in the Senate, and needed to reclaim only one seat to reclaim the supermajority lost in the 2024 elections. local.title: Morelle re-elected. Here's what could await in the next Congress
local.summary: Voters returned Morelle to a fifth term and a possibly elevated national role focused on elections and anti-corruption measures.
local.body:
U.S. Rep. Joe Morelle was elected to a fifth term Tuesday, and will return to a Democratic majority in Congress.

"Now the hard work begins to restore trust for the American people that people in government are looking out for their interests," Morelle said. "And we're going to get to that work immediately."

Morelle defeated Republican challenger Virginia McIntyre, vastly outspending the Monroe County legislator and taking 62% of the vote in the Democrat-leaning district, according to unofficial tallies from the state Board of Elections. The district covers Monroe and extends into Ontario County.

In the nearby 24th District, which surrounds Monroe County, voters backed Republican Claudia Tenney's re-election bid by a slightly smaller margin over Democratic challenger Alissa Ellman.

Morelle's comments about next steps alluded to his expected role in the next Congress, championing a package of anti-corruption bills he helped to pen that could be the first legislation Democrats put forward. The Associated Press called the House majority for Democrats after 1 a.m. Wednesday, and called the Senate earlier in the night.

"If I'm blessed to have the chairmanship of the committee on House Administration, which looks tonight like that's likely, I'm going to work on putting an end to stock trading for members of Congress and people in the administration and the Supreme Court," the Irondequoit lawmaker said. "I'm going to put an end to people participating in the prediction markets. I'm going to put an end to dark money and make sure people are disclosing the influence of billionaires in our politics, and make sure that we reform campaign finance."

Morelle's campaign disbursements topped $2.1 million, including transfers to other candidate committees, and he had $468,000 cash on hand as of mid-October, according to federal campaign finance records . McIntyre's outlay was $66,000 — with her last financial disclosure showing her campaign nearly $11,000 in the red.

"I just would have liked it to have been tighter to really drive it home that you don't need that money and that power in order to run," McIntyre said. "You know, I think that we need fresh blood. We need fresh voices in there, and I want to make sure that they're not dissuaded from seeing the results tonight."

entertainment.body:
Nicki Minaj made an Election Day appearance at a polling station in Derry, N.H., on Tuesday (Nov. 3). The rapper didn’t make any public statements during her police escort around Pinkerton Academy, but she did briefly interact with voters.

“Welcome to New Hampshire, Nicki. You look beautiful,” an onlooker shouted, according to NBC News . “Thank you,” Minaj replied.

Another woman thanked the Queens rapper — who lives in the Los Angeles area — for her loyalty to the president. “Thank you for touring with the president. I was most impressed,” a voter said. Minaj shook the fan’s hand and took photos with others at the polling site. “My pleasure,” Minaj can be heard saying in a clip shared by NBC News.

According to the outlet, Minaj appeared around 5:30 p.m. ET on Tuesday and left in an unmarked van with a police escort.

The 43-year-old hasn’t been shy about her adoration for Donald Trump and aligning with the Republican Party throughout 2026. Ahead of midterms, Minaj flew with Trump on Air Force One to a rally in Michigan in an effort to mobilize voters.

“President Trump, it is an honor to stand with you every single time,” Minaj said at the Port Huron rally on Oct. 25. “And I will continue to support you forever and ever. If you run again, I will support you again.”

Trump is currently without a White House press secretary, and the rapper’s name has been floated to fill the role. “That’s a good idea. I think I’ll have to think about that. I’m gonna think about that,” Trump said of the idea of Minaj joining his team during a late October appearance on The Benny Show .

Minaj criticized New York Gov. Kathy Hochul on Oct. 28, ahead of the politician’s reelection bid. “Kathy Hochul is an evil woman,” the rapper wrote on X. “The Democratic Party should forfeit her seat because even if she wins, she will be of great consequence to them. Downward spiral for her. She will not escape God’s wrath. She did not denounce evil when she had the chance.”

Cher seems unbothered by Michael Douglas’ recent swipe at her 1988 Academy Award win. entertainment.title: 25 Biggest Concert Residencies of All Time
entertainment.summary: From Celine and Cher to Elton and Bruno Mars, these are the highest grossing residencies in Billboard Boxscore history.
entertainment.body:
Each year, an uncountable number of recording artists transform their discographies into live shows, going on tour to super-serve their biggest fans around the world. But a select few have the power to bring their fans to them, staging extravagant productions in one city as the masses travel to see a once-in-a-career performance. Here, we’re looking at the biggest residencies in Boxscore history.

Most often, these residencies occur at theaters in Las Vegas. Among the most popular international tourist destinations, Sin City has become a second home for many of the biggest acts in music.

The biggest disruption to this list over the last handful of years has been arena-sized residencies, from the many acts who have sold out Sphere, to the conclusion of Billy Joel ‘s 10-year stay at New York City’s Madison Square Garden and most recently, to Celine Dion — once the queen of Vegas — heading across the pond for an ongoing string of shows at Paris’ Plenitude Arena.

Some ground rules: As with all Boxscore charts, this list includes only shows that were reported to Billboard Boxscore. The threshold for inclusion on this list is a minimum of 10 shows at a single venue. Some productions, especially those by MGM, will have a home base at a Vegas theater but travel to a handful of other venues, such as The Theater at MGM National Harbor in Oxon Hill, Md. — only the home-venue shows will count toward residency totals.

Further, this list includes only residencies that have their own unique names and productions and setlists — no mini-residencies within a tour. That means that Harry Styles ’ lengthy runs at MSG are excluded, as they were part of larger world tours. Same goes for the theater stints that made up Madonna ’s Madame X Tour in 2019-20 and Shakira ‘s recent 13 shows in Madrid.

However, residencies that are broken up by tours do count. That means that Bruno Mars ‘ Park MGM residency – interrupted by the 24K Magic World Tour – is eligible, as is Carrie Underwood ’s Reflection.

entertainment.body:
A hit song can be a gift and a curse. Yung Miami notched her first top 20 smash on the Billboard Hot 100 this summer with “Spend Dat,” and she parlayed the momentum garnered from the anthem leading into her debut solo album, Watch Dis , which arrived on Oct. 23 and debuted at No. 138 on the Billboard 200 . Explore Yung Miami See latest videos, charts and news

Miami recently stopped by Billboard News for an interview with Tetris Kelly, talking all things surrounding the success of “Spend Dat” and her star-studded project, which included feeling the pressure of her first hit. Related The Lettermen's Tony Butala Dies at 87 Karol G Sweeps Latin Airplay's Top 3 With 'No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto' Tracks Steve Ellis, Love Affair Singer, Dies at 76

“Just seeing the success of ‘Spend Dat,’ it gave me anxiety; I’m not gonna lie,” she admits. “I was excited, but I was like, ‘Damn, this is big.’ I want this album to just be great, which I feel like it was. It really made me go back and hone in. Make sure that the album was top to bottom the way I needed it to be.”

Miami continues: “Before ‘Spend Dat,’ I had a couple songs, and when I did ‘Spend Dat,’ I was like, ‘Nah, I gotta go back in.’ I think I know what the people want. I think I see the direction. After ‘Spend Dat,’ I did ‘2008,’ ‘F You’ and the Bryson [Tiller] record came after.”

The 32-year-old didn’t hold back on the collaboration side, notching assists from G Herbo , Travis Scott, Bryson Tiller, Quavo, Rick Ross, Summer Walker and more. In the interview, she highlights teaming up with Walker and Bryson as a couple of her favorite moments on the album.

“I know doing this album, I wanted some big features, but Summer Walker, I love Summer Walker. I’m a Summer Walker girl,” she shares. “When it comes to R&B, that’s my No. 1 girl. I love every album she ever put out.”

Miami then gushes about Bryson: “Always been a fan of his; I love his music. I love the way he communicates to women. I just love his voice. I just think there’s something about him that’s just unique.”

As far as a potential City Girls reunion with JT, Miami had a one-word answer: “Inshallah.”

entertainment.title: Tinto Brass, Director of the X-Rated ‘Caligula,’ Dies at 93
entertainment.summary: The Italian filmmaker clashed with screenwriter Gore Vidal during the making of the epic that starred Malcolm McDowell.
entertainment.body:
Tinto Brass, the Italian director best known for helming the X-rated Roman Empire epic Caligula , starring Malcolm McDowell, died Wednesday in Rome, his family announced. He was 93.

Brass started out in the 1960s with avant-garde films before he pivoted to erotic cinema, with his other features in the genre including Salon Kitty (1976), The Key (1983), Paprika (1991), All Ladies Do It (1992), Frivolous Lola (1998) and Cheeky (2000).

McDowell starred in the title role as the sexually deranged emperor in Caligula (1979), written by Gore Vidal and produced by Penthouse magazine founder Bob Guccione. The film, also featuring Helen Mirren, Peter O’Toole , John Gielgud and lots of orgies, was slammed by critics and audiences after its original release. Related Stories Oscars 2027: Int'l Films in Focus 'Ulya' Director Dives Into His Third Latvian Oscar Contender, Which Stars a Rising Actor as a Female Basketball Legend and Became a "Blockbuster" Movies BAFTA Breakthrough Ted Evans Shares What Sign Language Taught Him About Film - and What's Next After 'Retreat'

Brass and Vidal clashed during production and would disown the feature — the director was unhappy with the editing (done after he was fired), the screenwriter with how Brass rewrote his script. Caligula , however, gained a cult following over the decades, and a 178-minute “ultimate cut” version received a showcase at Cannes in 2023.

Born in Milan on March 26, 1933, and raised in Venice, Giovanni Brass earned a law degree, worked as an archivist at the Cinémathèque Française in Paris and served as an assistant director to Roberto Rossellini and Alberto Cavalcanti.

He made his feature directorial debut on Who Works Is Lost , which screened at the 1963 Venice International Film Festival, then helmed Yankee (1966), a Western, and the murder mystery I Am What I Am (1967), starring Jean-Louis Trintignant . (The last one received a 4K restoration and a screening at Venice in September.)

In 1970s, he won the Golden Bear at the Berlin International Film Festival for his surrealist comedy The Howl , which he also wrote.

Survivors include his second wife, Caterina, whom he married in 2017, and his children, Bonifacio and Beatrice. His first wife was Carla Cipriani; he was married to the daughter of Harry’s Bar founder Giuseppe Cipriani from 1957 until her death in 2006.

entertainment.summary: Wanna play?
entertainment.body:
Nicki Minaj may think that she and Chucky are friends ’til the end, but the creator of the iconic horror movie character begs to differ.

After the rapper shared what appeared to be an AI-generated image of the red-haired doll sporting a pink suit and a “Vote Red” badge — her way of encouraging fans to cast their ballots for Republicans on Election Day — filmmaker Don Mancini clapped back by setting the record straight on how his character would’ve actually voted on Tuesday (Nov. 3). (You know, if murderous children’s toys could legally participate in elections.)

“Chucky has a trans kid,” Mancini wrote on X , sharing a photo of a real-life Chucky doll holding a Glenda figurine. “Chucky protects the dolls. Chucky is anti-ICE. Chucky says ‘A BLUE WAVE’ is coming, as BLUE as my f–kin’ eyes!”

Glenda, who sometimes goes by Glen, is indeed a canonical character in the Child’s Play franchise. The offspring of Chucky and his doll “bride” Tiffany, Glen(da)’s gender and expression are fluid in the movies — something many conservatives might take issue with, considering the Republican party’s notoriously intolerant policies on issues such as trans rights and gender-affirming care.

“Too bad, Nicki!” Mancini added after Democrats took back control of both the Senate and House of Representatives on Tuesday in addition to winning numerous local elections, resharing his previous photo of Chucky edited with blue hair. “No AI, by the way! #bluewave”

Minaj’s love for Chucky goes back years, with the Queen of Rap famously spitting on her verse on Ye’s “Monster”: “And I’ll say, bride of Chucky, it’s child’s play/ Just killed another career, it’s a mild day.” In 2019, she and husband Kenneth Petty — who in 2022 was sentenced to three years’ probation and a year in home detention after failing to register as a sex offender in relation to his 1995 conviction for attempted rape in the first degree — dressed up as Tiffany and Chucky for Halloween.

She’s also favored using photos and memes of Chucky on social media over the years, including but not limited to her posts taunting Democrats in the past year or so since she publicly joined the MAGA movement . “HAPPY ELECTION DAY!!!” she wrote on X on Tuesday alongside the AI rendering of Republican Chucky.

The hip-hop star hasn’t posted since the results of the election. She last dropped music in 2024, reaching Nos. 23 and 68 on the Billboard Hot 100 with Megan Thee Stallion diss track “Big Foot” and Juice WRLD posthumous duet “AGATS2 (Insecure),” respectively.

entertainment.summary: EloElo Group said it raised new equity funding, including from the Hollywood studio, to help its Story TV platform launch phone-focused mini-series internationally, including in the U.S. market.
entertainment.body:
NBCUniversal and Hornbill Capital have led an $80 million Series C fundraising round for Indian microdrama producer EloElo Group, founded by former Flipkart executive Saurabh Pandey.

The new capital will allow the Story TV platform operator to produce new vertical dramas for export internationally, including to the U.S. market. The Series C investment, usually done to allow startups to scale operations, follows NBCUniversal’s Peacock streaming platform launching the unscripted vertical series, Campus Confidential: Miami , as part of a wider push into mobile content to reach new audiences.

“At NBCUniversal, we see significant opportunity in mobile-first storytelling and emerging formats like micro dramas to engage audiences and meet evolving viewing habits. Under Saurabh’s leadership, EloElo has developed a differentiated, mobile-first approach with a clear focus on content and storytelling, positioning the company for long-term success. We’re excited to bring NBCUniversal’s global capabilities to the partnership as EloElo expands beyond India, including into the U.S. market,” Deepak Arya, executive vp of corporate strategy & development at NBCUniversal, said in a statement.

EloElo Group, which launched in Bengaluru, India in 2020, points to an expanding slate of over 5000 micro dramas in six languages, while a Dolphin AI agentic production engine. Across its apps, EloElo Group added it has over 40 million monthly active users.

“This Series C deepens our content across languages, with a sharper focus on premium originals, doubles down on Dolphin AI, and takes what we have built to more audiences and more markets,” Pandey, founder and CEO of EloElo Group, said in his own statement.

Microdramas, which are typically produced in 60-90 second episodes and strategically written with a hook, a spike and a cliff hanger to get viewers onto the next episode, have caught on in North America and elsewhere internationally after coming out of China during the pandemic era.

entertainment.title: The Chicks Celebrate Democrats’ Historic ‘Blunami’ Midterm Election Victory With Two-Word Message to President: ‘F–k Trump’
entertainment.summary: The country trio could not have been more excited to see Republicans suffer massive losses on Tuesday night (Nov. 3) during their show in Los Angeles.
entertainment.body:
The Chicks were doing a happy dance on Tuesday night (Nov. 3) during their show at the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles as the midterm election results began to trickle in. The Texas-bred country trio, who have often been at odds with the Trump administration — including calling the former reality TV star a “ deranged nut job ” at a show earlier this year — celebrated the loud, widespread rebuke of Trump’s chaotic second term with a short, sharp, two-word message emblazoned on large red folding hand fans they held up with pride during the gig.

“ F–k Trump ” they read, according to a picture posted by the group on their Story. “Well, hello Los Angeles. Welcome to our blunami night,” lead singer Natalie Maines said during the show as the trio fanned their faces with the profane message, according to The Independent . “So glad we can enjoy this night together. Texas is blue, The Senate is blue. The House is blue. This was gonna be a very different night if that wasn’t the case. Welcome to the 20th anniversary of Taking the Long Way .”

The fans, and comments about the blue wave, came on a night when American voters sent a loud and clear message to Washington, rebuking the first two years of Trump’s second term. Voters seem to sour on the Republican administration after being roiled by seesaw, price-spiking tariffs, a deadly, widespread immigration crackdown, a war of choice with Iran that has led to massive increases in the price of gasoline and diesel and an affordability crisis Trump has deemed a “hoax” as he seems more focused on erecting gold-leaf monuments to himself across D.C.

The news was especially exciting for The Chicks — which also includes singer/multi-instrumentalists Martie Maguire and Emily Strayer — because their home state elected James Talarico as the first Democrat to win a Senate seat in the deep red state since 1994. Talarico easily best Trump’s preferred candidate, scandal-plagued state Attorney General Ken Paxton.

The blue wave resulted in seven Senate seats flipping, securing a majority for Democrats in the upper house, as well as a massive win in House races, with Democrats slated to take over both chambers on Congress in the new year. The solid majority in the House — which stood at 228 to 139 in Democrats’ favor at press time, with NBC predicting a potential 255-seat majority — is seen by many pundits as a referendum on Trump’s many unpopular policies, one that could lead to a swarm of investigations into the administration and the Trump family’s massive wealth gains over the past 18 months.

entertainment.title: Inside the Business of Boy Bands — From One Direction to BTS
entertainment.summary: On the latest episode of On the Record, Billboard's Jason Lipshutz joins the podcast to talk about his new book on One Direction and what makes boy bands a singular music business phenomenon.
entertainment.body:
For about as long as the recorded music industry has been around, so has fans’ obsession with male vocal groups. Now collectively referred to as “boy bands,” these groups have ranged in musical style, presentation and size across generations, but they always remain a mainstay in global music culture.

Groups like New Kids on the Block , Menudo , Boyz II Men , One Direction and BTS are more than just singers — they’re big business, and the music industry knows it. It’s become expected that modern hit boy bands can sell millions of albums and, at the same time, they can sell themselves — whether that’s emblazoned on pillowcases, t-shirts, action figures, toothbrushes and more.

But the way record labels can capitalize on the rabid fandom induced by boy bands doesn’t last forever. As Jason Lipshutz, co-chief content officer at Billboard , puts it in his new book A Whole Lotta History: One Direction and the Sound That Shaped a Generation, the groups are known to be “ephemeral” in nature, lasting for just a handful of years while their largely teen girl fanbase is at its most dedicated. “The idea is that if you’re 13 and a huge boy band fan, you know, by the time you’re 17, you might not be as into that boy band,” Lipshutz explains.

Lipshutz joins the latest episode of Billboard On the Record to talk about his new book on One Direction, the industry mechanics behind boy bands and how our modern definition of these groups came to be.

What is a boy band? Before that term got popularized in around the late ’80s, early ’90s, it was basically just, like, an all-male vocal group. And now, in the 2020s, we have this much wider understanding of what a boy band means, what is typically associated with it, how many members are in it and what the sound is like. Dating back to the ’60s, a boy band, before they were called a boy band, was basically just any kind of vocal group that was comprised of all men.

For generations before us, that was big business back then. And now, as popular culture has evolved, so has the idea of a popular boy band. I think the classical understanding of a boy band really is steeped in the ’90s — Backstreet Boys , *NSYNC , New Kids on the Block, et cetera.

Probably New Kids on the Block. I mean, you know, I think after the Beatles , you get to different iterations of that type of fan impact. In the ’70s, you have these family bands — the Jackson 5 and the Osmonds . What I write about in the book is that the great thing about the Beatles when they really first started is that they were coming off of this period where Elvis was king, and what the Beatles did was, for all of the fans who idolized Elvis, “Oh, now you can idolize this group of guys and pick your favorite and argue with your friends about your favorite.” In the ’70s, you have groups like the Jackson 5 and the Osmonds. Menudo starts in the ’70s. There you are also getting different members that fans gravitate toward because they’re of their ages.

entertainment.summary: Upgrade, CAA Media Finance and Range Select are pitching the high-concept horror film from director Ry Russo-Young to buyers at the American Film Market next week.
entertainment.body:
Daisy Ridley , Sosie Bacon and Simon Rex are set to star in Get Rid of It , a horror project that Ry Russo-Young will direct from a script by Gemma Holdway. Production is scheduled to begin at the start of the first quarter of 2027.

Ridley will play Harper, who discovers she is pregnant after a one-night stand with a drifter named Miller, played by Rex. Bacon will play Harper’s sister, Jessie. The sisters set out on a cross-country road trip and find themselves fighting for survival when they learn that what is growing inside Harper may not be human. Ridley will next be seen in Ti West’s Ebenezer , opposite Johnny Depp. Her earlier credits include Zak Hilditch’s We Bury the Dead , Joachim Ronning’s Young Woman and the Sea and the role of Rey in the most recent Star Wars trilogy.

Bacon currently stars opposite Nicole Kidman and Jamie Lee Curtis in Elizabeth Sarnoff’s series Scarpetta. She recently appeared in the SXSW title Family Movie alongside Kevin Bacon, Kyra Sedgwick and Travis Bacon. Her earlier work includes Parker Finn’s Smile and Brad Ingelsby’s series Mare of Easttown.

Rex played Mikey in Sean Baker’s Red Rocket . He has also starred in Nic Pizzolatto’s Easy’s Waltz and Zoë Kravitz’s Blink Twice .

“This project’s strength is its compelling point of view and heart beneath the horror,” Russo-Young said. “I’m thrilled to bring it to life with such an extraordinary and gifted group of collaborators.”

Russo-Young previously directed the sci-fi teen thriller Before I Fall , starring Zoey Deutch, and the drama The Sun Is Also a Star , with Charles Melton. She has also directed episodes of the Apple TV+ series Shrinking, which stars Harrison Ford and Jason Segel.

David Lancaster, whose producing credits include Whiplash , Nightcrawler and Drive , is producing. Upgrade, CAA Media Finance and Range Select are handling sales and will present the project to buyers at the fall market.

entertainment.title: What Abdul El-Sayed’s Wild, Historic Ride to the Senate Means to One Michigander
entertainment.summary: It's one race. But sometimes that's all it takes.
entertainment.body:
I’m just a Great Lakes boy, standing in front of his home state, asking for some clarity. And, perhaps, I’m a little closer to getting some.

Dr. Abdul El-Sayed , the Michigan native fond of exercising the right to bare (his impressive) arms , has just won my home state’s messy Senate race by six points. This is a boon to Democrats’ legislative goals — and to my own mental health. Because, in an admittedly myopic move, I decided early on that he would be the one candidate to whom I’d pin all of my 2026 hopes. Not just because he’s a litmus test for non-coastal Americans’ appetite for progressive politics. Because I deeply needed to know if my complicated home state was capable of electing a loud, liberal, practicing Muslim to such a high office. Related Stories News Trump Crashes Out After Democrats Flip House and Senate, Slams Fox News and Texas' Greg Abbott News Elon Musk Responds After His Record $474 Million Bet on Republicans Ends in Blowout

My doubts were not without merit. I spent my adolescence in deep red Livingston County, in a smallish town with exceptional public schools and a storybook Main Street that now has shops that sport trans pride flags in their widows and hosts an annual and very well-attended Gilmore Girls festival. Last December, mid-Hanukkah, that same Main Street was bombarded with white supremacists carrying signs that read “Happy Holidays, Heil Hitler” while reportedly spicing up their antisemitic campaign by calling passing holiday shoppers the n-word and the f-slur.

Mike Rogers, El-Sayed’s MAGA-endorsed opponent, grew up in Livingston County as well. And he represented our town during his years in the Michigan State Senate before going on to represent those same constituents in the House of Representatives. My dad couldn’t stand him. Still can’t. And I vividly recall rolling my eyes under the brim of my marching band hat (it’s called a Shako!), whenever I had to watch Rogers gladhand the town’s Republican majority at football games as he made his leap to national politics. What I wouldn’t learn for another 25 years is that El-Sayed’s grandparents were helping to raise Abdul just a few miles away. Because Livingston County is also home to Jan and Judy Johnson, the newly famous TV stars whose series of campaign spots for their grandson epitomize the kind of Michiganders who I know and come from.

OK, that was arguably too much color about one random cluster of towns an hour’s drive west of Detroit. But if this much paradox can exist within this 15-mile radius, how can anything but an election like the one we’ve just had tell me where the majority of people’s heads and hearts are at? Because I didn’t grow up in the only culturally bipolar part of Michigan or any other state. This country is a real trip, and most of us realized that before 2016.

entertainment.title: Trump Crashes Out After Democrats Flip House and Senate, Slams Fox News and Texas’ Greg Abbott
entertainment.summary: "I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!" the president claimed in one post on Truth Social.
entertainment.body:
After Democrats flipped the U.S. House and Senate on Tuesday night, it’s safe to say President Donald Trump wasn’t too thrilled.

Hours after the polls closed and it was revealed that Democrats won some surprising races in the 2026 midterms, including for the Texas, South Carolina and North Carolina Senate, Trump took to Truth Social hours after the polls closed with several posts, slamming Fox News and Republican Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, who lost re-election to Democrat Gina Hinojosa .

“If Greg Abbott, the Governor of Texas, hadn’t become a RINO in the last six months of his Political Life, he wouldn’t have lost,” he wrote in one post. “He went back to his original formula, and it wasn’t pretty!” Related Stories News Elon Musk Responds After His Record $474 Million Bet on Republicans Ends in Blowout Midterms 2026 Hollywood Sat Out the Billionaire-Tax Fight. Its Workers Could Pay the Price.

Trump added in another, “Why does FoxNews have Bill de Blasio, the Worst Mayor in the History of New York City, on air, ranting and raving like a Lunatic? He left the City in disgrace, and the damage he caused was incalculable — It has never been the same, and now he’s telling us how to run America. FoxNews bears responsibility for these losses by constantly and consistently putting on the Dumocrat opposition, and worse. GOD BLESS AMERICA!”

Along with posting a photo of his signature red caps, with the word “VETO” displayed on it, he also wrote , “I’m going to become a Political Pundit, both good and bad, on the reasons these Candidates won and lost!”

Earlier in the evening, as it started to become clear that it was going to be a big night for Democrats, Trump initially claimed that he would have won in a landslide if his name was on the ballot. “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE! Thank you for your attention to this matter,” he wrote on Truth Social.

However, Trump wasn’t eligible to be on the 2026 ballot as he’s currently the sitting president of the United States. He also can’t run again in 2028, as the 22nd Amendment of the U.S. Constitution limits any person to being elected to the presidency twice, and Trump was already elected in 2016 and 2024.

While Trump appears furious at the midterm results, he also told The New York Times shortly before 10:30 p.m. on Tuesday that he’s “absolutely willing to accept” them.

entertainment.title: Jason Sudeikis Takes on Fatherhood, Green Pigs in New ‘Angry Birds Movie 3’ Trailer
entertainment.summary: Josh Gad, Danny McBride, Rachel Bloom and Keke Palmer also lend voices to the Paramount animated sequel to hit theaters on Dec. 23.
entertainment.body:
Jason Sudeikis lends his voice to saving the world as a red-feathered and bewildered father in the latest trailer for The Angry Birds Movie 3 that dropped on Wednesday.

“It’s time to suit up. Let’s save the world as a family,” Sudeikis reprising his role as Red in all his mighty cardinal plumage says at one point in the new movie teaser.

In The Angry Birds Movie 3 , Red navigates the challenges of fatherhood, rallying his family — including partner Silver (Rachel Bloom), kids Glider (Walker Scobell), June (Emma Myers), Olly (Psalm West), and their pet Fuzzy (James Austin Johnson) — with a pasta party before embarking on their next chaotic adventure. Related Stories Music Jisoo to Release Original Song for Upcoming 'The Angry Birds Movie 3' (Exclusive) TV Samuel L. Jackson's 'Tulsa King' Spinoff 'Frisco King' Sets Premiere Date in First Teaser Trailer

“Er, Silver, can you please tell our daughter to be a little less gross at the table?” a baffled Red asks before setting out to save the island, yet again, from mysterious green pigs.

Josh Gad returns as the voice of Chuck, while Danny McBride reprises his role as Bomb. Red’s pals join the fun in The Angry Birds Movie 3, the newest installment in the animated franchise that began with 2016’s The Angry Birds Movie and its 2019 sequel.

The feature is based on the popular video games from Rovio Entertainment, a subsidiary of Sega . The ensemble voice cast for Angry Birds Movie 3 also includes Marcello Hernández , Tim Robinson, Lily James , Keke Palmer , Anna Cathcart, Maitreyi Ramakrishnan, Nikki Glaser, MrBeast , Salish Matter and Sam Richardson.

John Rice directed the film based on a screenplay by Thurop Van Orman, with John Cohen, Dan Chuba, Carla Connor and Namit Malhotra producing. Rovio Entertainment, One Cool Group, Dentsu Entertainment, Flywheel Entertainment, Prime Focus Studios and John Cohen Production are producers on the film.

The Angry Birds Movie franchise kicked off in May 2016 and centered on an island of flightless birds dealing with the arrival of a group of pigs. Sony Pictures released the first two films, including 2019’s The Angry Birds Movie 2 , which have collectively surpassed $500 million at the global box office.

entertainment.title: Thaddea Graham to Be Honored at the Oscar Wilde Awards (Exclusive)
entertainment.summary: ‘The Bad Sisters,’ ‘Margo’s Got Money Troubles’ and ‘Artificial’ actress will be feted March 11 in Los Angeles.
entertainment.body:
Thaddea Graham, the actress from Northern Ireland known for her turns on Sex Education at Netflix and Bad Sisters and Margo’s Got Money Troubles at Apple TV, will be honored at the 21st annual Oscar Wilde Awards .

Organized by the US-Ireland Alliance, the event is set for March 11 at the Ebell in Los Angeles in its traditional evening spot three days before the Academy Awards. It celebrates the work of those who are Irish — and some who are not — who contribute to film, television and music.

Irish American actor Jack Reynor was announced last month as an honoree. Guests also will be treated to a performance by the Irish synth-pop singer Shobsy. Related Stories Movies 'Joy Will Prevail,' Starring Griffin Dunne as Architect Louis Kahn and Alexis Bledel, Tells the Story of the Director's Childhood Home (Exclusive PÖFF Trailer) Movies 'La Bola Negra' Wins Another Prize -- London Film Festival's Audience Award

Graham, 29, will receive the Wilde Card Award, “which is presented to someone we expect you’ll hear a lot more from,” US-Ireland Alliance president Trina Vargo said. Previous honorees include Saoirse Ronan, Barry Keoghan, Sarah Bolger and Bad Sisters actress Eve Hewson.

Graham last year appeared alongside Julia Roberts, Ayo Edebiri, Andrew Garfield and Michael Stuhlbarg in Luca Guadagnino’s After the Hunt , and she has reunited with the Italian director on the upcoming hot-button film Artificial , which stars Garfield as OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.

She also played the personal assistant of George Clooney’s actor character in Noah Baumbach’s Jay Kelly (2025).

Graham was discovered as a baby on the steps of a building in Changsha, China, when she was a few days old. She was adopted at 13 months and brought by her parents to County Down as one of the first Chinese-born children adopted in Northern Ireland.

“I always say I would not be here had it not been for the kindness of strangers,” she told The London Times in April. “From the earliest days of someone stopping and seeing I’d been left, picking me up and looking after me, I’ve seen that kindness throughout my life, from my parents, who are wonderful, through school and the support of my teachers. My primary-school teacher introduced a Chinese New Year celebration, which she continues even though I’m not there anymore.”
